item.title: [source] Barbarians at the Gate: The Fall of RJR Nabisco (Burrough and Helyar, 1990)
item.description: Wall Street Journal reconstruction of the 1988 fight for RJR Nabisco: Ross Johnson’s management LBO, Shearson, Kohlberg Kravis Roberts, Forstmann Little and First Boston, through the November 30 special-committee decision. HarperBusiness Essentials EPUB of the 1990 Harper & Row book.

item.title: [source] Overnight Success: Federal Express and Frederick Smith (Trimble, 1993)
item.description: Vance H. Trimble’s biography of Frederick W. Smith and Federal Express—Memphis Smith family transportation fortune, Yale and Vietnam, Little Rock aviation rescue, hub-and-spoke overnight package concept, Falcon fleet and purple livery, venture capital and Colonel Crown, 1974 forgery crisis and trial, first profits, Memphis hub drama, and 1980s expansion through the Flying Tiger pursuit.

item.title: [source] Rickover: The Struggle for Excellence (Duncan, 2001)
item.description: Francis Duncan’s authorized biography of Adm. Hyman G. Rickover—Maków origins and Naval Academy, destroyer and submarine duty, Engineering Duty Only and BuShips electrical section in WWII, Oak Ridge and the joint AEC–Navy nuclear propulsion program, Nautilus and Shippingport, national-figure years under Eisenhower–Kennedy, Thresher and two-year extensions, nuclear carriers and Los Angeles-class fights, shipbuilding claims, Carter partnership, 1982 retirement, death in 1986, and engineering legacy.

item.title: [source] Grinding It Out: The Making of McDonald’s (Kroc with Anderson, 1977)
item.description: Ray Kroc’s autobiography (with Robert Anderson)—Lily Tulip paper-cup and Multimixer sales apprenticeship, 1954 San Bernardino meeting with the McDonald brothers, Des Plaines franchise launch, Harry Sonneborn’s real-estate financing model, Fred Turner’s operations discipline, buyout of the brothers, public company growth, personal upheavals, and San Diego Padres ownership through the mid-1970s.

item.title: [source] Vision: A Saga of the Sky (Mansfield, 1956)
item.description: Harold Mansfield’s narrative history of the Boeing Airplane Company from William E. Boeing’s 1910 Dominguez Field encounter through Claire Egtvedt, Phil Johnson, and Bill Allen—mail planes, pursuits, all-metal Monomail/247, Flying Fortress and B-29 Superfortress, Battle of Kansas, postwar swept-wing B-47/B-52, Stratocruiser, 707 jet transport, and Bomarc missiles—framed by engineer John Haberlin’s thirty-year banquet speech.

item.title: [source] The Snowball: Warren Buffett and the Business of Life (Schroeder, 2008)
item.description: Alice Schroeder’s authorized biography of Warren Buffett—Nebraska lineage and Omaha childhood, Washington wartime paper routes, Columbia and Ben Graham, Buffett Partnerships and Berkshire Hathaway, See’s/GEICO/Washington Post, Susie and Astrid, 1980s deal culture and Salomon, with Sun Valley/tech-bubble and twenty-first-century philanthropy chapters as continuity.

item.title: [source] Call Me Ted (Turner with Burke, 2008)
item.description: Ted Turner’s autobiography (with Bill Burke)—Cincinnati childhood and McCallie, Brown and Coast Guard, Turner billboards and father’s 1963 suicide, WTCG/SuperStation, Atlanta Braves, America’s Cup, CNN and Headline News, Goodwill Games, CBS and MGM fights, cable-operator rescue, Jane Fonda and land conservation, with 1990s–AOL chapters retained as forward continuity.

item.title: [source] Apollo: The Race to the Moon (Murray & Cox, 1989/2004)
item.description: Charles Murray and Catherine Bly Cox’s engineering-and-operations history of Apollo—not astronaut celebrity biography but how NASA’s Space Task Group, ASPO, Marshall, the Cape, and Mission Control built and flew the moon program from 1958 through Apollo 13 and program close.

item.title: [source] Empire / Howard Hughes: His Life & Madness (Barlett & Steele, 1979)
item.description: Donald L. Barlett and James B. Steele’s investigative biography of Howard Hughes—from Hughes Tool inheritance, Hollywood extravagance, and 1930s aviation records through World War II defense contracts, the Spruce Goose, and the 1947 Senate investigation, then postwar RKO, TWA, Las Vegas, Watergate/Hughesgate, CIA Project Jennifer, and the 1976 death and estate fight.
